Parāmāsagocchaka (The Group on Misapprehension)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.

Dependent on a state that is an object of clinging, a state that is not an object of clinging arises by way of root condition: dependent on clinging, the associated aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.
Dependent on a state that is not accompanied by lust, a state that is not accompanied by lust arises by way of root condition:

dependent on one aggregate not accompanied by lust, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … two aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking … (up to the great primary elements of non-percipient beings).

Dependent on a state that is not grasping (no-parāmāsa), a state that is grasping (parāmāsa) arises by way of root-condition (hetu-paccaya): dependent on aggregates that are not grasping, grasping [arises].
Dependent on a state that is not grasping, states that are both grasping and not grasping arise by way of root-condition:
dependent on one aggregate that is not grasping, three aggregates, grasping, and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] …
Dependent on a state that is neither grasping nor non-grasping, a state that is non-grasping arises by way of root condition:

dependent on one non-grasping aggregate and grasping, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … pe … dependent on two aggregates … pe … dependent on grasping and the great primaries, mind-produced matter arises.
In the Pure Cause Section:
five in the root condition, five in the object condition (five in all cases), one in the resultant condition …pe… five in the non-disappearance condition.
Positive Order.
2.9.1.1.2. Negative Analysis of Conditions:
The Section on Exposition (Vibhaṅgavāra).
Dependent on a state that is neither a cause nor associated with lust, a state that is neither a cause nor associated with lust arises by way of the root condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate not associated with lust, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on].
At the moment of rootless rebirth-linking …pe… (up to non-percipient beings),
in dependence on aggregates associated with doubt and associated with restlessness, there arises delusion associated with doubt and associated with restlessness.
Not-object condition.

Dependent on a state that is an adherence (*parāmāsa*), a state that is not an adherence arises by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*): dependent on adherence, mind-produced matter arises.

Dependent on a state that is not an adherence, a state that is not an adherence arises by way of the object-condition: dependent on the aggregates that are not adherences, mind-produced matter arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [and so on] ... up to the non-percipient beings.

Dependent on both misapprehension and the state that is not misapprehension, a state that is not misapprehension arises by way of object condition: dependent on misapprehension and its associated aggregates, mind-produced matter [arises].

One [condition] with respect to root, one with respect to object, three with respect to predominance, three with respect to proximity, three with respect to contiguity, one with respect to conascence, one with respect to mutuality, one with respect to dependence, one with respect to strong-dependence, one with respect to prenascence, one with respect to postnascence, one with respect to repetition, one with respect to kamma, one with respect to nutriment, one with respect to faculty, one with respect to jhāna, one with respect to path, one with respect to association, three with respect to dissociation, three with respect to presence, three with respect to absence, three with respect to disappearance, and three with respect to non-disappearance.

**Hetu-duka (Root-pair):** With root condition, there are three with respect to non-object, five with respect to non-predominance ... pe ... five with respect to non-resultant ... pe ... three with respect to non-association, five with respect to non-dissociation, three with respect to non-absence, and three with respect to non-disappearance.
2.2. Analysis of the Negative Section on Conditions (Paccayapaccanīya Vibhaṅgavāra):
The Non-root Pair (Nahetuduka)
With non-root condition: one [mode] in the object, one in the immediate, (one in all cases), and one in the non-disappearance. 2.9.1.2.
The Chapter on Conascent Conditions:
The chapter on conascent conditions is also similar to the chapter on dependence.
2.9.1.3. Section on Conditions (Paccayavāra) 2.9.1.3.1.
Positive Enumeration of Conditions (Paccayānuloma Vibhaṅgavāra)

Conditioned by a state that is grasping at causes (*hetu-parāmāsa*), a state that is not grasping arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*): conditioned by grasping, the associated aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.
Conditioned by a state that is not grasping, a state that is not grasping arises by way of root-condition: [conditioned by] a state that is not grasping...

Conditioned by one aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … pe … conditioned by two aggregates … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … (down to) the internal great primaries; conditioned by the [heart-]base, aggregates that are not objects of clinging arise.

Conditioned by a state that is not an object of clinging, a state that is an object of clinging arises by way of root condition: conditioned by aggregates that are not objects of clinging, clinging arises; conditioned by the [heart-]base, clinging arises.
Conditioned by a state that is not grasping, states that are both grasping and not grasping arise by way of root condition:

conditioned by one aggregate that is not grasping, three aggregates, grasping, and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … conditioned by two aggregates … [and so on] … conditioned by the physical basis, grasping arises; conditioned by the great primary elements, mind-produced matter arises.
With the object as condition, there arise both the perversions and the associated aggregates.
With a state that is both a perversion and not a perversion as condition, a state that is not a perversion arises by way of root-condition:
with one aggregate that is not a perversion and a perversion as conditions, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … two.
Conditioned by the aggregates …pe… and by the perversion together with the associated aggregates, mind-produced matter arises;
conditioned by the perversion and the great primaries, mind-produced matter arises; conditioned by the perversion and the [heart-]base, the non-perverted aggregates arise. (Abbreviated.)

In the Pure Root Condition: five; in the Object condition: five; in the Predominance condition: five (five in all cases); in the Resultant condition: one …pe… in the Non-disappearance condition: five.

Conditioned by a state that is not accompanied by rapture, a state that is not accompanied by rapture arises by way of the not-root condition:

conditioned by one rootless aggregate not accompanied by rapture, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … [continue] … up to the non-percipient beings; conditioned by the eye-base, eye-consciousness arises.
...pe... conditioned by the body-base, body-consciousness arises; conditioned by the [heart-]base, rootless aggregates free from lust arise;
and conditioned by doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied aggregates and the [heart-]base, doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied delusion arises. (Abbreviated.)

under the Pure [Dependent] Relation: one for not-root, three for not-object, five for not-predominance, three for not-proximity … pe … none for not-strong-dependence.
Three [in the case of] not-prenascence; five in not-postnascence; five in not-repetition; three in not-kamma; five in not-resultant;
one in not-nutriment; one in not-faculty; one in not-jhāna; one in not-path; three in not-association;

2.9.1.3.4. Negative-Positive Conditionality (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma)
With not-root condition, one [formula] for object ... pe ... one for non-disappearance. 2.9.1.4.
The Section on Support (Nissaya-vāra):
The section on support is the same as the section on conditions.

2.9.1.5. Section on Conjoined States (Saṁsaṭṭhavāra) A state conjoined with, but not adhered to by, a state adhered to arises by way of root condition: the aggregates associated with and conjoined to the adherence.

(In this manner, five questions are to be formulated, and these apply only to the formless realm; the section on conjoined states and the section on associated states are to be formulated in this same way.)

…pe… doubt … restlessness … grief arises; [or] formerly well-performed deeds …pe… having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna …pe… noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path, review the fruit, and review Nibbāna.

with that as object, lust … doubt … restlessness … and grief arise.
With the divine eye, one sees a form; with the divine ear-element, one hears a sound.
